newsitem.title: USA: US investors expect Brazil Brady swap size to grow.
newsitem.headline: US investors expect Brazil Brady swap size to grow.

text.p: Brazil's Brady bond swap dominated emerging debt markets on Tuesday, as portfolio managers juggled their options and awaited the pricing of the country's 30-year global bond later the same day.
Market talk circulated that the global bond swap, initially set at $1.0 billion, might grow to $2.0-$3.0 billion and be issued at 370-380 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries.
"They want good after-market demand for this, so I think they are still going to price at 370-375," said one U.S. proprietary trader.
Last month, Brazil offerred to exchange its Par bonds, Discount bonds or "C" bonds for a global bond, or to allow direct purchases of the new issue. The offer expired June 3.
The critical issue will be how large Brazil allows the issue to grow and how this size affects the demand curve, U.S. investors said.
"The interesting question is going to be the size and whether they go for spread or not," one investor said.
An analyst at one U.S. mutual fund said that 375 basis points was on the cusp of attractability, and added that 385 would be more appealing.
"My hope is that they'll give a few extra pips to the buyers," the analyst said. "They should be generous. They should make the market feel good."
The market expected heavy demand for the global bond and major cutbacks in the cash tranche, leading the global to tighten by 30 basis points after pricing, one investor said.
Regarding the various investment options, investors said their strategies fluctuated over which option to select as market prices changed daily.

"I've gone back and forth on this so many times, right now I think discounts are the better instrument," said one investor who specialized in Brazil. "It's a sign prices are fluctuating narrowly around the exchange set ratios, which is what you would expect."
One analyst said that investors holding "C" bonds would probably not tender any paper.

Spreads of Brazil Bradys over U.S. Treasuries tightened in Tuesday morning trade. The benchmark "C" bond added 1/4 to 79-3/4 bid, while pars were unchanged at 66-3/8, and discounts were up 3/8 to 83-3/8.
